summary: Milestone 2026.05.241 had no experiment commits recorded in the timing data window; 0 experiments completed and 0 wall-time minutes logged. Both RTX 3090 GPUs were idle at 0% utilization with only 5 MB allocated each, consistent with a milestone that ran no compute-bound tasks.
bottlenecks_identified: No experiments were activated or completed this milestone — the primary bottleneck is milestone activation itself, not experiment execution speed.

Both GPUs (GPU 0: RTX 3090, GPU 1: RTX 3090) are idle at 0% utilization with residual 5 MB allocations, suggesting a prior session left stale CUDA contexts that were never freed. This is a minor housekeeping issue, not a wall-time bottleneck.
improvements_suggested: Ensure the research-roadmap-next.yaml is present and valid before milestone activation so the conductor can begin launching tasks immediately rather than falling through to a zero-experiment milestone.
Free stale CUDA memory allocations (5 MB on each GPU) between milestones to avoid confusing future GPU-state snapshots — run `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset` or restart the holding process.
Add a pre-activation check in the conductor that warns if the roadmap YAML is missing or stale; log a WARN rather than silently producing a zero-experiment milestone.

DualGPURunner engagement is not applicable this milestone (no parallel-model tasks ran), but both GPUs are free for the next milestone — plan at least one dual-model inference task to recoup the idle capacity.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Confirm research-roadmap-next.yaml exists for milestone 2026.05.242 with a valid milestone: field and at least one activated task before closing this retrospective — a pre-staged roadmap is the single highest-leverage action to avoid another zero-experiment milestone.
Free the 5 MB stale CUDA allocations on both GPUs so the next milestone starts with a clean GPU state and the GPU Monitor does not flag spurious idle-with-allocation warnings.

Wire a conductor pre-activation guard that halts and notifies the operator when experiments_activated == 0 at milestone open, preventing silent zero-progress milestones from consuming calendar time without any research output.
meta_reflection: A zero-experiment milestone is a process failure, not a research failure — the conductor ran but nothing was activated, so there is nothing to optimize at the experiment level. The actionable finding is upstream: roadmap presence and activation-guard coverage must be confirmed before a milestone opens, not discovered in the retrospective after it closes. GPU and compute efficiency analysis cannot be performed when no tasks ran; all three questions in this retrospective reduce to 'no data available this milestone.'
